subject: economics (most rules hold for any subject taught by concepts, causes and numbers)
status: LOCKED by Navin on 4 November 2026 ("sab lock kar dun"). Learned from 37 Indian-economy reference videos (about 4 h 35 min); EV-U04, EV-L09, EV-L10, EV-S08, EV-S09 and EV-G02 added the same day from batch 4 (20 more videos), and EV-U05, EV-L11 to EV-L14, EV-S10 to EV-S13, EV-R02 and EV-G03 from batch 5 (12 more, E58–E69), locked under Navin's standing approval of 4 November under the agreement's section 8 (the videos teach every section of BIE).
evidence: asset_intake/econ_kit on branch asset-intake: canvas cards (how each idea was shown), teaching cards (how it was taught, 848 speech-picture tiles with word timings), show lexicon, needs list. Numbers in the rules are measured there.

rules.rule: Teaching order is not page order: open each concept with the problem, need or puzzle it answers, then name it, then define it. Recall the earlier idea it stands on before using it (half of the reference videos open by recalling the previous idea).
rules.check: Does each concept open with the problem or need it answers, and is its prerequisite recalled before it is used?

rules.rule: Cut a topic with the strategy that fits the concept: an instrument (bond, bill, swap) - follow one of it through its life (issue, promise, risk, resale, return) and bring each term at the step that needs it; a cause or a real-vs-nominal idea - hold one small market or one product fixed and change one thing at a time; a series of rules or tools - problem, answer, its limit, the next problem; a policy goal - ask 'what does this depend on?' backwards until a lever appears, and name control of that lever; a whole and its parts - name the term where the parts disagree with the whole; a new pair of terms - teach it through a pair the learner knows; an exception - build the normal rule first, then the case that breaks it; competing definitions - test each on a small made-up country until its numbers break; a dense official definition - cut it into phrases, each phrase one step of a worked example; a national total - scale up from one person to a family to the country.
rules.check: Does the lesson's order follow one of these cutting strategies for the kind of concept it teaches?

rules.rule: History of institutions: cut at each law or committee; before each law ask the question it answers; then the law, then the institution or change it made, then the result, all on one running timeline that returns as the recap.
rules.check: In a history part, does every law come after the question it answers and before the change it made, on one timeline?

rules.rule: Scene first, term after: a small situation, role-play, made-up market or surprise shows the effect before the term is said (in the references the story comes about 30 s before the term). A later explanation of failure points back to a moment of that scene.
rules.check: Is every new term said only after a scene or example has shown what it names?

rules.rule: Right after a term is said, one 'yaani' line opens it in plain words (an English term gets its everyday Hindi meaning and who uses it).
rules.check: Is every new term followed at once by a plain-word line?

rules.rule: One running example carries the lesson: small round numbers, one thing changing at a time, the same actors and numbers to the end. Every derived number must agree with the example's arithmetic.
rules.check: Is there one running example with small numbers whose arithmetic holds everywhere it is used?

rules.rule: Say the learner's objection out loud ('aap kahenge ...', 'lekin ...') and answer it; give the turn its own beat.
rules.check: Is at least one natural learner objection voiced and answered per concept that invites one?

rules.rule: End every step with one conclusion line ('to yahan saaf hua ...') before moving on; signpost each new branch ('chaliye ab ...'); deliver every promised agenda item or say it comes later.
rules.check: Does each step end with a conclusion line, and is every promised item delivered or deferred?

rules.rule: Every number on screen is spoken and every spoken number is on screen, with the same value; a big number gets a felt size (a reserve as months of imports, a crowd as 140 crore people).
rules.check: Do the spoken and on-screen numbers match one for one, and does each big number get a felt size?

rules.rule: Say what the change means for a person: what they gain, lose or feel (can sleep easy, the bank shuts its doors).
rules.check: Does each mechanism end with what it means for a person?

rules.rule: Recap over the last teaching picture before any question for the next video; never over an end card.
rules.check: Is there a recap over a teaching picture before the close?

rules.rule: Show the step, not the word: every spoken mechanism, rule, analogy and cause is shown by things acting (a pattern of the show lexicon), not by writing its name or the sentence. In the references only 37% of picture changes show the meaning and 46% only write words; BIE aims for most.
rules.check: Does each mechanism, analogy and cause line have a picture that acts it out rather than a label or sentence?

rules.rule: A thing appears on the word that names it: from 1 s before to 0.5 s after the word (in the references the median is 0.14 s before and 73% land within 1 s). An object may lead by up to 2 s; text never more than 3 s early.
rules.check: Does every element appear within about 1 s of the word that names it?

rules.rule: Keep one scene and change one part per idea; mark what changed. A change of system reuses the same picture (only a tag, a ring or the arrow direction changes; arrows flip when authority changes).
rules.check: Is a change shown on the same picture with only the changing part moving?

rules.rule: Follow one object through a calculation or a chain (one egg through a price index, one bond through its owners) before the rest join it.
rules.check: Does a calculation or chain follow one visible object step by step?

rules.rule: No decorative motion while teaching (a spinning globe, waving flags) and no frame unchanged for more than about 15 s while the voice speaks; spoken direction words (rise, fall, more, less) match what moves.
rules.check: Is the picture free of idle motion, never frozen over 15 s of speech, and does every spoken direction match the motion?

rules.rule: Showing patterns for economics (show lexicon): giving, paying or lending - the thing travels from hand to hand on the verb, the return on a dotted arrow; a two-way deal - paper one way, cash the other, a frame closes around both; a share kept aside - a slice splits off into a vault; risk moving - a RISK disc slides from one party to the other; a rate change - strike and replace with an arrow; many buyers - a crowd grows or shrinks; reach - a shaded share of one crowd; classes - real items gather, then snap into labelled groups; tiers - boxes inside boxes; a law - the paper drops at its year and an arc runs to what it made; institutional history - merge, rename, move and ownership zone on a timeline; authority - arrows from the decider; problem and fix - crosses then ticks on the same chips; failure - return arrow crossed and a FAIL stamp; total of parts - parts stack into the whole; growth - a tiny thing becomes a huge one; a peg - a rope ties one note to another; a gap - a longer bar beside a shorter one, the gap becomes a named block; permission - a licence is a gate things pass through; comparison - mirror pictures, one difference at a time.
rules.check: Does each line that matches one of these kinds of idea use its pattern or a better picture?

rules.rule: Institutions are shown by institutionBadge or a generic building with a name plate (centralBank for the RBI); never a real logo, emblem, seal, real landmark or real person.
rules.check: Are all institutions shown without real logos, emblems or persons?

rules.rule: Numbers are read exactly as shown on screen, units included; the voice slows a little on a new term and on the number that carries the point.
rules.check: Are numbers read as shown, and do new terms and key numbers get a slower delivery?

rules.rule: A level is built from the lesson's own running example, and the mechanic fits the concept: a process to run (the most common in economics), things to place into groups (place_right), a cause chain, a timeline to build, the student acting as the institution or person who decides (act_as), or setting a number first and seeing the real one (predict); every wrong move shows what breaks and why, using the same picture as the lesson.
rules.check: Does each level reuse the lesson's running example, and does every wrong move show what breaks and why?

rules.rule: One question per concept, answered by the shape that fits it: a flow for a process or cause (most common), a comparison or table for differences, a picture for a mechanism, a timeline for history, a tree for classes, a number for a calculation; the answer reuses the lesson's picture and running example.
rules.check: Does every concept have a notes question whose answer shape fits it and reuses the lesson's picture?

rules.rule: Exam practice: each statement is checked against the one concept that decides it; a false statement is crossed and every option containing it is crossed too (elimination shown, not told).
rules.check: Do practice items link each statement to its deciding concept and show elimination?

rules.rule: Reviewers check by code where possible: spoken and on-screen numbers agree; the running example's arithmetic holds; spoken direction words match the motion; no overlay or end card covers teaching; every agenda item promised at the start is delivered.
rules.check: Do spoken and on-screen numbers agree, does the example's arithmetic hold, do spoken directions match the motion, is no teaching covered by an overlay, and is every promised item delivered?

rules.rule: Teach in layers and say so: first the everyday picture that is enough for anyone, then the exam layer ('UPSC ke liye thoda aur gehrai mein'); related measures (GDP, GNP, NDP, NNP; CPI, WPI, food index; headline and core) are taught as one world with one running example in which each measure is one filter, addition or subtraction on the same numbers.
rules.check: Are the layers announced, and are related measures built on one shared example?

rules.rule: Every question put to the viewer is answered before the video ends, and every loop opened (a promised comparison, an unexplained figure, an open 'why') is closed; a number in an exam-style question that is not used is explained.
rules.check: Is every question to the viewer answered and every opened loop closed?

rules.rule: A definition is cut word by word into its parts and each part becomes one small rule with its own example (GDP: market value, final, goods and services, within the country, in a period), with a visible step counter.
rules.check: Is a dense definition taken apart word by word, each part with its own example?

rules.rule: More showing patterns (economy batch 4): which items count under a definition - each item travels to a gate or the map and gets a tick or a cross; a measure that leaves parts out - a segmented bar whose parts are crossed and removed so the bar closes up; ownership changing over funding rounds - money comes in, a share certificate goes out and the founder's share is struck and rewritten each round; a rising cost of borrowing - a staircase of % tags above the lender; a hedge - one price path with profit and loss regions and the two positions netted in one tag; equity - a highlight that spreads from a few people to the whole crowd; pooling - many investors' notes go into one cart or fund; a conversion between currencies - a foreign note goes into a converter and a rupee note comes out; measures compared - contestants on a stage, one judging question per round.
rules.check: Does each line of these kinds use its pattern or a better picture?

rules.rule: A spoken story with actors gets its own scene with those actors acting it; never narrate a story over a frozen diagram (the references froze for 35-95 s during stories). Nothing covers the teaching picture: no banner, promo or end card while teaching continues.
rules.check: Does every spoken story have its own acted scene, with nothing covering the picture?

rules.rule: Game ideas the economy videos suggest, to build from the chapter's own example: be the counter at the gate (count or do not count into GDP); be RBI with a rate or a reserve (act_as); split deposits into CRR, SLR and loans and see the income (predict); be the founder choosing debt or equity round by round; hedge a holding against news; give growth money to health, education or defence and see the crowd's development meter.
rules.check: Does the game use one of these ideas where the chapter has the matching concept?

rules.rule: Successive systems, institutions and reforms (PLR to BPLR to base rate to MCLR; IFCI to the state DFIs, ICICI, IDBI and SIDBI; nationalisation to the 1991 reforms): each one enters as the fix for the previous one's named problem and leaves with the evidence that it fell short (one number: a 1.25-point cut reached loans as 0.6), which is the next one's problem. Give the lens first (a U-turn, a pendulum) before the details, and the map of categories only after the story (E58).
rules.check: Does each system in a sequence open with the problem it fixes and close with the evidence of its shortfall?

rules.rule: Right after a definition, show one near miss that is not the term, crossed, and say why (one or two goods getting dearer is not inflation); the boundary finishes the definition.
rules.check: Does a definition get one near miss that is crossed with its reason?

rules.rule: A lever (a ratio, a rate, a tax) is run both ways in the same picture, less and more, and each way is followed to the same end variables (lending, prices, the exchange rate); a fork saancha carries the two ways with their conditions and results.
rules.check: Is every lever run both ways to the same end variables?

rules.rule: Build a mechanism by hand with the running example before its name or formula (the multiplier round by round: 1000 becomes 2500 at a 40% reserve), then test it with one what-if (10% gives 10 times); the name and the formula come as the summary of what was just done.
rules.check: Is the mechanism computed with the example before its name and formula, and tested once with a what-if?

rules.rule: Two mirrored cases (a price rise at home and abroad; an export story and an import story; a person's crisis and a country's) are told in the same picture, then joined into one rule, then the rule is applied once to an exam-style question; the term (PPP) is named only after it is calculated.
rules.check: Are mirrored cases told in one picture, generalised, then applied to one exam question?

rules.rule: Measures built from parts (M0 to M4, a price basket, NDTL): lay out the whole as its parts first; each measure is a row of ticks in a table saancha; a measure built on another copies that row and adds one tick; the column a definition leaves out glows.
rules.check: Are measures built as rows of parts, each new one copying the row it is built on?

rules.rule: Show an equivalence before saying it: two routes to the same result end in the same picture (the same hands, the same tags: printing money ends where the tax ended), then name the one difference (one is announced, the other is not).
rules.check: Do two equivalent routes end in the same picture before the equivalence is said?

rules.rule: Histories, reforms and life cycles sit on one timeline saancha that gains an event per step (upto) and marks the one being told (at), with periods as bands; a lesson with several parts keeps a roadmap saancha at the side whose current item moves on; never a new slide per law or per part.
rules.check: Is a history on one growing timeline, and a multi-part lesson on one moving road map?

rules.rule: A diagram the voice builds is built on screen at the voice's speed: graph lines draw themselves (drawIn) while the curve is described, table rows appear (upto) as each is said, a formula's terms arrive one by one; nothing is pre-drawn and read off. In the batch-5 references 104 of 111 segments were a plain canvas: a world (a place) is used for stories and processes that happen somewhere, a diagram for everything else.
rules.check: Is every diagram built at the speed of the narration, and a place used only where something happens there?

rules.rule: Direction words on rates agree with the numbers (depreciation means more rupees per dollar; a cut makes the number smaller), and the hook's promised number equals what the example produces (the references promised 4 times and showed 2.5); time-bound facts (which rate is the floor, ownership limits) are checked for the book's date and a changed fact is flagged in the review record, never on the learner's screen.
rules.check: Do rate direction words match the numbers, does the hook's number match the example, and are changed time-bound facts flagged in the record?

rules.rule: More game ideas from the economy videos: be the bank splitting each deposit between the CRR vault, the SLR safe, loans and parking at RBI (a bank-hall world level); be RBI moving the repo under a base-rate or an MCLR rule and watch the pass-through meter (predict); be the finance minister filling the gap by tax or by printing (act_as: printing raises the price tag and quietly shrinks every hand); be the exporter under each year's exchange-rate card; run the multiplier rounds until the money supply meter stops; choose the door to enter or leave a fund (open or close-ended).
rules.check: Does the game use one of these ideas where the chapter has the matching concept?
